data: UN Tourism collects, standardizes and publishes statistics of tourism, and promotes the integration of these statistics within the sphere of the United Nations system
Data are collected and updated on a regular basis through questionnaires to country statistical focal points.

The definitions and classifications used are based on the International Recommendations for Tourism Statistics 2008 (https://www.unwto.org/tourism-statistics/on-basic-tourism-statistics-irts-2008), approved by the United Nations Statistical Commission at its 39th session (26-29 February 2008).

NOTE: The results presented are based on a newly implemented data collection process, based on a new unified questionnaire. The corresponding new data processing system is currently in a transitional phase, and therefore some data points may not yet fully reflect the intended standards. We appreciate your understanding as we continue the ongoing improvements, which are also expected to gradually increase the completeness of the datasets.

The data and related materials provided by UN Tourism are made available “as is” and reflect the most current information accessible at the time of publication. UN Tourism does not warrant, guarantee, or make any representations (express or implied) regarding the accuracy, reliability, completeness, timeliness, or fitness for a particular purpose of the content.

While every effort is made to ensure the quality and consistency of the data, this dataset is part of an evolving process. Opportunity areas have been identified to enhance coverage, harmonization, and methodological consistency. Future updates may include refinements to validation procedures and improvements in data structure.

UN Tourism shall not be liable for any direct, indirect, consequential, or incidental damages arising from the use or inability to use the data or related materials. Users are encouraged to interpret the information within its intended scope and context."
